ocr_text: <ocr>LORILLARD, INC. � ONE PARK AVENUE, NEW YORK, N.Y. 10016-5895 �(212).545-3000 RONALD S. GOLDBRENNER Associate General Counsel (212) 545-3353 Via Telecopier: I Timothy K. Hoelton, Esq. Harley-Davidson, Inc. 3700 West Juneau Avenue P.O. Box #653 Milwaukee, WI 53201 September 3, 1993 Post-It"" brand fax transmittal memo 7671 Fof pages . ~ imoth K. Hoelte  From, R. Goldbrenner oftarley-Davidson oO' Lorillard Dept. Phone lk 12-545-3354 Fax N 414-935-44 4 Fax t1 Re: Lorillard/Harley-Davidson Trademark License Dear Tim: I am writing to follow up on our telephone conversation earlier today, in which we agreed to meet on Tuesday, September 7 in New York to discuss the current impasse between our two companies regarding the advertising for Harley-Davidson cigarettes. In our discussion, I requ5:~sted that you bring -ith you to the meeting the market research data referred to in your August 27 letter and also in the compiaint that was filed in Milwaukee after we filed suit in New York. Harley claims that this research proves that Lorillard's proposed advertising campaign appeals to "underage children." You have stated that you would not turn over your market research data, except as may be required by Lorillard's Subpoena Duces Tecum. As we have related to you and others at Harley, we are at a loss to understand the true nature of your objections because we do not believe that the advertising we have used or contemplated for use with HD cigarettes directs its appeal to children. If your market research data validly shows this to be the case it seems to us you would want us to see it and I can assure you that it would substantially advance our ability to consider settlement. Moreover, since the data will have to be disclosed in discovery by Sept. 13, 1993, we urge you to reconsider and provide it on Tuesday, Sept. 7. In a prior conversation, you stated that you desired to see the market research data you had requested in exchange for pgNbr=1 14 the KRC study. As I explained the two are not at all on the same footing. As we told you, during our meeting of Aug. 12, 1993, Lorillard does not conduct cigarette market research with children and so none was done in focus groups or in any other manner. We give very explicit instructions to all our suppliers not to conduct such market research. All research is directed to .adults. In light of your concern we have given instruction to recheck this matter and confirm our original understanding. We urge you to reconsider and disclose your KRC study. It would also be helpful if you could have a representative of KRC available, who is familiar with the research and who might help us assess its proper significance. Very truly yours, . g.%AaA. ~--~ Ronald S. Goldbrenner Sr pgNbr=2 </ocr>
